summary: A Codex seat on the default profile resumes its saved thread; before, the resume failed and the seat started a new one

replay.detail: No stored history or replay change.

schema.detail: No database, claim or configuration schema change.

rules.detail: No checkpoint rules or coordination version change.

compatibility.detail: Codex 0.160.1 refuses permission config on a remote resume (Permission overrides are not supported when resuming a remote task). st's automatic-resume argv for the remote TUI kept the -c entries of the default profile (default_permissions, permissions.*, approvals_reviewer, sandbox_workspace_write.*), so a restarted plain-declaration Codex seat on an auto install had its TUI exit and the driver fell back to a new session. The resume argv now drops those entries; the app server still holds them and thread/resume selects the profile. A seat whose declaration carries authored permission arguments is also affected, for the better: an authored -c entry for default_permissions, approval_policy, approvals_reviewer or sandbox_mode used to make a resume fail the same way, and now leaves the TUI argv and is projected through thread/resume together with the authored -s, -a, model and effort. Authored sandbox_workspace_write.* entries and permission profile definitions stay on the app server only; thread/resume does not carry them.

manual.detail: None. A seat that already lost its thread to the fallback keeps its old Codex rollout file on disk; it is not reattached.

recovery.detail: Reverting restores the failure on resume for plain-declaration Codex seats on an auto install.
